sections.h2: Who to call about property tax
sections.html:
Two county offices work out of the Administration Building, 2 South Second Street, Harrisburg. The Office of Tax Assessment sets and maintains assessed values at (717) 780-6101. The Tax Claim Bureau collects delinquent real estate tax at (717) 780-6125. Both are open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., though the Bureau stops taking payments at 4:00 p.m.

The county does not send the current year's bill. Each of the county's 39 municipalities passes unpaid accounts to the Bureau through its own tax collector or treasurer. To find out who collects your current bill, ask the County Treasurer's office or your municipal office.

One bill covers three levies, since the county, your municipality and your school district all tax the same parcel.

The county's January 2026 millage sheet lists a county rate of 9.193 mills in every district and a 0.35 mill library rate in most. Municipal and school rates then vary. Combined totals run from about 27.8 mills in Middle Paxton Township up to 58.97 mills in Highspire Borough. The assessment ratio is 100% across the county, Harrisburg included.

School rates are the 2025/2026 fiscal rates set in July 2025. Some municipalities add charges for hydrants, street lights, sewer or trash on top of the listed rate.

Harrisburg uses a split municipal rate: 30.97 mills on land and 5.16 on buildings, plus a 30.78 mill school rate.

File with the Board of Assessment Appeals after June 1 and by 4:30 p.m. on August 1. Appeals that arrive later are rejected, even if they were mailed before the date.

A new or changed assessment during the year has its own window: the appeal must be received within 40 days of the date on the change notice. The Board meets at the Administration Building, second floor. Mail goes to PO Box 1295, Harrisburg, PA 17108-1295, and the phone is (717) 780-6102.

  • There are five appeal forms: single family residential, residential multi-family or apartment, farm, commercial or industrial, and exempt.
  • The owner, an authorized representative or a lessee who pays the tax signs. A corporation signs through an officer.
  • Every parcel carries a filing fee, paid by check or money order to the Board and never refunded.
  • No appeal is heard while delinquent taxes remain on the parcel.
  • Only a Pennsylvania attorney may represent an owner, and the person appealing is expected at the hearing.

Ask the Board for the fee that applies to your property class.

An unpaid account moves to the Tax Claim Bureau, which collects delinquent real estate tax for the county, the municipalities and the school districts. The Bureau adds a $20 fee per tax due.

It takes cash, certified checks, cashier's checks and money orders. Cards work online or by phone at a 2.55% fee, or $4.00 for Visa debit. Personal and business checks are sent back. A missing notice is not an excuse, so keep your mailing address current with the Tax Assessment Office.

Some districts are collected elsewhere. Portnoff Law Associates handles Steelton Borough and the Steelton-Highspire School District from the 2018 tax, and Highspire Borough and Lower Paxton Township from the 2024 tax. CGA Law Firm handles Penbrook Borough from the 2024 tax. If you own in Lower Paxton or Highspire and owe back tax, call the right collector first.

The Bureau also runs upset sales, judicial sales and the repository of unsold properties.

Order a tax certification before you list. It is an official letter from the Bureau stating whether delinquent tax is due on the parcel, with a claim statement showing the amount on that date. The cost is $15 per parcel.

  • Pay the back tax at or before closing so the title company can issue clear title.
  • Request a tax sale abstract only if a sale has already happened. It is $25 per parcel, per sale, and lists the notices and the purchaser.
  • Use certified funds for a large payment, since personal checks are refused.
  • Ask the municipal collector whether the current year's tax is paid, because that bill is separate from the Bureau's.

Clearing the balance before a sale keeps the Bureau from moving the parcel toward an upset sale. A cash buyer does not change any of this: the taxes still have to be settled, and the title company will want the certification in hand. Allow time for the Bureau to issue it, and for the payoff, before the closing date is set.

Act 29 of 2026, House Bill 858, created a county-maintained contact registry for non-owner-occupied property. Owner-occupied principal residences are exempt.

An owner of a rented or vacant property must give the assessment office a name, address, phone number and email for someone authorized to fix code violations. The first filing is due within 30 days of taking ownership, and updates are due within 30 days of any change. Failing to comply can bring a $500 fine. Lenders can be covered after a sale or foreclosure.

The Tax Assessment office accepts the owner contact form by mail, by email or in person. A landlord who sells should file the update or confirm that the new owner has filed.

The county had an estimated 293,351 residents in July 2025 and 129,660 housing units. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $236,400 for 2020 to 2024, and 63.1% of homes are owner-occupied. Median household income is $76,242 and median gross rent is $1,217.

Because the assessment ratio is 100%, assessed value tracks market value closely, and the district you are in drives the size of the yearly bill. Buyers comparing a house in Middle Paxton Township with one in Highspire Borough will see very different carrying costs, and your agent should be ready to explain yours. Have your latest bill on hand when you talk about price.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal a Dauphin County assessment?
faqs.a: August 1 at 4:30 p.m. is the cutoff for annual appeals, and filing opens June 1. A late appeal is rejected even if mailed on time. Changed assessments during the year have a 40 day window from the notice date.

faqs.q: What is the county property tax rate in Dauphin County?
faqs.a: The county rate is 9.193 mills in every district, with a 0.35 mill library rate in most. Municipal and school rates are added, so district totals run from about 27.8 to 58.97 mills.

faqs.q: Who collects delinquent property tax in Dauphin County?
faqs.a: The Tax Claim Bureau collects it, with a few exceptions. Portnoff Law Associates and CGA Law Firm handle certain boroughs and Lower Paxton Township. The Bureau adds a $20 fee per tax due.

faqs.q: How much is a tax certification in Dauphin County?
faqs.a: A tax certification costs $15 per parcel. It states whether delinquent real estate tax is due, and a claim statement shows the balance as of that date. A sale abstract is a separate $25 per parcel.

faqs.q: Does Act 29 of 2026 apply to me?
faqs.a: It applies if you own non-owner-occupied property such as a rental or vacant house. You must register contact details with the assessment office within 30 days of ownership. Owner-occupied principal residences are exempt.
